Run 0006's own pre-registered 'midday regression => reconsider' trigger also fired (16h lap 19.18->15.07). Cost 12/68 = 18% of review-class bursts sent since 07-28 (~1-2 alerts/night); latency cost ~0 in practice (Daniel labels in batches hours later). Shipped alongside Part B, the symmetric retention purge (human_retention_proximity_seconds, 240 s, either direction) so a misclassified person burst no longer keeps recognisable frames past the 48 h human-photo policy. See runs/0010 night 4.

ACTIVATED + SHIPPED 2026-09-02 (commit 2f469fa). Loop-side code only -- live on the NEXT nightgate invocation, no camera restart and no env delta. The loop could not report its own death: loop.nightgate heartbeats ONLY on gated-out ticks, so (a) a tick that PASSES the gate and then dies is completely silent -- the 27-night OAuth outage 2026-08-04..29, found only because Daniel looked -- and (b) nothing checks the camera at all, so the ~20h manual-stop outage 2026-09-01 19:13 -> 09-02 15:14 was silent too. Fix: two independent best-effort checks in nightgate, run on EVERY tick (proceed or skip -- the outage was on PASSING ticks, so a skip-only check would have missed it): loop staleness (days_behind(last_tick_completed_day, loop_day()) > 2 -> alert, stamped once per loop-day in last_staleness_alert_loopday; threshold 2 not 1 so a single normal missed night never pages) and camera liveness (systemctl is-active wildlife-camera.service != active -> alert, stamped in last_camera_alert_loopday). Both wrapped in try/except that logs and continues: neither can change the gate's exit code or raise out of main(), so a broken alert path degrades to the OLD behaviour (silence), never to a broken gate -- the key constraint, since nightgate is the one component whose death silences everything downstream. Decision logic is 3 pure functions (days_behind, should_alert_staleness, should_alert_camera_down) tested without I/O. 550 tests pass (was 532). Replayed against both real incidents: both fire. Live smoke test on a copy of real state: proceeds, exit 0, no alert, no Telegram -- state is exactly 2 days behind and '>2' is correctly false at the boundary. FN-veto N/A (touches no detection/classification/mute/routing path). RESIDUAL GAP, not solved: the switch lives INSIDE nightgate, so it cannot fire if the timer itself stops -- and the 2026-09-01 tick never ran at all. That needs an off-Pi watchdog and is explicitly not claimed here. Rollback: git revert 2f469fa, no restart. See runs/0013.

REJECTED AS DESIGNED 2026-09-02 -- the pre-registered fix was re-measured before shipping, as the protocol requires, and the measurement REFUTED it. Do not re-derive it. The release trigger opened on 08-31 ('ship as the first act of the tick that concludes exp #14') fired on this tick and was correctly spent on re-validation, not on shipping. Pre-registered design was a score floor on the human gate's homo-taxon arm (SPECIES_HOMO_TAXON_MIN_SCORE=0.75), sited in what night 1 read as an empty trough between an 'adjudicated-empty' low mode (<=0.66, 17/17 bursts empty) and a 'confirmed-people' high mode (>=0.85). The 09-01/02 window contains 34 taxon-arm HUMAN rows with pc<0.50, 17 of them low-mode, ALL 17 with frames on disk and ALL 17 adjudicated: SIX CONTAIN REAL PEOPLE -- 4907 (0.549), 4840 (0.599), 4897 (0.617), 4845 (0.631), 4850 (0.673), 4848 (0.674); 4840/4848 show two adults full-frame and plainly identifiable. Empties occupy 0.579-0.731, people occupy 0.549-0.674: the two classes are COMPLETELY INTERLEAVED and no in-BOUNDS floor separates them. Night 1's bimodality was a sampling artifact of a quiet day with almost no human traffic, not a property of the signal. Counterfactual over the window: 4897 (person at close range, 2186s after the previous surviving HUMAN burst, density 0, no HUMAN burst inside the 240s deferral) would have been SENT TO REVIEW -- every layer of the proximity/density/deferral stack is blind to it. That is a rollback event under exp #14's own standing rule, so it must not be deployed in the first place. WHAT SURVIVES: the phantom half of the finding is confirmed and strengthened -- 11 of 17 low-mode taxon rows are empty garden and they do arm real mutes (4828 armed two; 3 of 9 proximity mutes in the window were phantom-armed). WHAT IS REFUTED: that the ensemble's homo-taxon score can tell people from empty scenes. Any future attempt needs a DIFFERENT DISCRIMINATOR, not a different threshold. Absent one the taxon arm stays unthresholded, because the failure mode of leaving it alone (a muted empty scene, costing observability) is strictly cheaper than the failure mode of demoting it (a person's photo in REVIEW). See runs/0012 'Backlog #16 ... REFUTED'.

OPENED 2026-09-04. The Scene-Unchanged Gate is effectively INERT in the current scene and its threshold is still unvalidatable, both now MEASURED rather than assumed. (a) Inert: on 2026-09-04 the camera fired 48 times at one static pond scene; 45 review-class bursts recorded scene_similarity min 0.664 / median 0.887 / MAX 0.944, so T=0.97 could not fire once. Corpus-wide the gate has muted 25 bursts since it was enabled 2026-07-26 and 0 in the last 5 days. (b) The metric is illumination/time-drift dominated, not subject-presence dominated: within-burst frame1-vs-frame5 pairs of the SAME scene seconds apart score median 0.968 (max 0.990), while cross-burst pairs of the same scene minutes-to-hours apart top out at 0.944 -- and a person filling the frame (bursts 4945/4946) scores 0.474-0.739, which OVERLAPS the empty-scene band's low end (0.664). So the score mostly measures how long ago the reference was taken. (c) FN evidence, first datapoint ever: burst 4516 (2026-08-16, IDENTIFIED animal, the only animal burst with frames still on disk) scores 0.931 against the empty reference immediately preceding it -- INSIDE tonight's empty band. Lowering T to 0.93 would have muted a real animal, so the FN-veto now has positive evidence, not just absence of evidence. T stays 0.97. SHIPPED THIS TICK (commit f14ed0d, restart-gated 09-05T03:25): scene_similarity is now measured and DB-logged for EVERY status, not only review-class, so the animal bucket can finally fill from IDENTIFIED rows; scene_gate_muted and the reference-set update stay review-class-only, so no routing changes (FN-veto N/A by construction). PROMOTION CRITERION: once >=5 IDENTIFIED (or human animal-labelled) rows carry a scene_similarity, apply the protocol's rule T = max(animal sims) + 0.02 clamped to BOUNDS [0.80,1.0]. If that lands above 0.97 the gate should be RAISED (it is currently too permissive on paper and inert in practice); if below, the gate is not usable in this scene and disabling it is the honest call. Do not lower T before that bucket exists.
